request: What are the estimated budget costs of clean energy tax credits?

reply.reply:
**CRS’s table provides selected clean-energy credit estimates, including $13.1 billion for the residential clean energy credit over FY2023–FY2027; it does not establish a single total cost for all clean-energy tax credits.**

- CRS reports an estimated $13.1 billion cost for the residential clean energy credit over FY2023-FY2027. (R46865, PDF p. 6)
- The cost estimates generally use JCT tax-expenditure estimates for FY2023-FY2027, reflect laws enacted through August 31, 2023, and assume temporary provisions expire as scheduled. (R46865, PDF p. 3)
- JCT estimated the sustainable aviation fuel credit would reduce federal revenues by $49 million from FY2022 to FY2026, although it was omitted from its latest tax-expenditure reports. (R46865, PDF p. 28)

Not yet covered: A comprehensive total across all clean-energy tax credits is not confirmed by the recorded evidence; the cited estimates may cover only selected provisions.
reply.reasoning: The CRS report gives provision-level tax-expenditure estimates and explains the period and assumptions behind them. The evidence retrieved supports one specific credit estimate but not an aggregate across all clean-energy credits.
